title: Logical Backup Restore
summary: An accidental delete removed part of a customer accounts table, but a recent logical backup snapshot is available for selective recovery.
incident: 15:05 — A maintenance script accidentally deleted 250 customer account rows. A read-only logical backup snapshot from shortly before the incident still contains all 2,000 records. Restore only the missing rows, preserve valid live data, and leave the backup source untouched.
objectives: Compare the live table with the backup snapshot.
Identify exactly which account IDs are missing.
Restore only the missing rows rather than replacing the whole live table.
Verify row counts and balance totals match the backup after recovery.
hints: Compare IDs with a LEFT JOIN or NOT EXISTS query before restoring anything.
The backup snapshot is read-only by design; restore into the live table.
An INSERT ... SELECT with NOT EXISTS can restore only rows that are actually missing.

setup_sql: CREATE TABLE customer_accounts (id BIGINT PRIMARY KEY, customer_name TEXT NOT NULL, balance_cents BIGINT NOT NULL CHECK (balance_cents >= 0), status TEXT NOT NULL); INSERT INTO customer_accounts(id, customer_name, balance_cents, status) SELECT gs, 'Customer ' || gs, 10000 + (gs * 37 % 250000), CASE WHEN gs % 11 = 0 THEN 'review' ELSE 'active' END FROM generate_series(1, 2000) AS gs; CREATE TABLE customer_accounts_backup AS TABLE customer_accounts; ALTER TABLE customer_accounts_backup ADD PRIMARY KEY (id); DELETE FROM customer_accounts WHERE id BETWEEN 751 AND 1000; CREATE TABLE incident_notes (id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY, note TEXT NOT NULL); INSERT INTO incident_notes(note) VALUES ('A logical snapshot was taken before the accidental delete and contains 2,000 accounts.'), ('Exactly 250 live rows are missing: restore them selectively.'), ('Do not overwrite valid live rows or modify the backup snapshot.');

statements: GRANT SELECT ON customer_accounts_backup, incident_notes TO {learner}

checks.name: All customer accounts restored
checks.feedback: The live table still does not contain exactly 2,000 customer accounts.

checks.name: No backup account IDs are missing
checks.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM customer_accounts_backup b WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM customer_accounts a WHERE a.id = b.id)
checks.feedback: Some account IDs from the backup snapshot are still missing from the live table.

checks.name: Live balances match backup
checks.sql: SELECT (SELECT sum(balance_cents) FROM customer_accounts) = (SELECT sum(balance_cents) FROM customer_accounts_backup)
checks.feedback: The restored live balance total does not match the backup snapshot.

checks.name: Backup snapshot preserved
checks.feedback: The backup snapshot must remain intact with all 2,000 rows.

evaluation.success_feedback: The missing customer accounts were selectively restored, live balances match the backup, and the recovery snapshot remains intact.
